text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
Business:
ADEVARUL
- Parliament's lower Chamber of Deputies set an 18 percent tax on income from house and office renting.
- The government blacklisted 222 state-run companies leading bad debtors including 6,700 enterprises which take 70 percent of losses in the economy and 60 percent of inter-enterprise arrears.
- Oil refineries Petrotel, Petrobrazi and Petromidia, tractor maker Tractorul Brasov and truck manufacturer Roman Brasov are among bad debtors blacklisted by the government.
- State-owned Banca Agricola gave farm credits worth 239 billion lei for the spring campaign.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- State-owned bank Bancorex signed an accord on a $75 million syndicated loan -- the first such deal for a Romanian commercial bank -- arranged by CS First Boston.
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- Romania revised estimates for the 1997 wheat crop down to 7.07 million tonnes, at an average yield of 2.9 tonnes per hectare.
- Tourism Minister Akos Birtalan wants to exempt local tour operators from VAT on tours abroad, to encourage indirect exports.
General:
ADEVARUL
- Reform of the main opposition Party of Social Democracy (PDSR) is blocked by rifts within the party, the newspaper's editorial says.
- Romania's Danube Delta drew only 13,600 tourists last year, from a 1979 peak of 89,000.
ROMANIA LIBERA

- Protests continue in the coal mining Jiu Valley area with striking miners marching across their Petrosani stronghold, shouting anti-government slogans. A government delegation is expected to start talks with miners' leaders on Friday.
- President Emil Constantinescu summoned economic ministers and ruling coalition leaders in a bid to defuse tension in the Jiu Valley.
- Miners accross the country might start protests and block roads in solidarity with striking Jiu Valley miners, labour union leader Marin Condescu said.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- Some 7,000 wood industry workers marched through Bucharest on Thursday asking for pay rises, improved living standards and soft loans for their sector.
- Romania's ex-King Michael and Bulgaria's ex-King Simeon plan a meeting of exiled monarchs from eastern Europe.
-- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
